title: Time Based Key-Value Store
statement:
Design a time-based key-value data structure that can store multiple values for the same key at different timestamps and retrieve the key's value at a certain timestamp.

Implement the `TimeMap` class:
- `TimeMap()` initializes the object.
- `set(key, value, timestamp)` stores the key `key` with value `value` at the given `timestamp`.
- `get(key, timestamp)` returns the value associated with the largest `timestamp_prev <= timestamp` for which `set` was previously called on `key`. If there is no such value, returns `""`.

Because timestamps passed to `set` for a given key are strictly increasing, each key's stored values form a sorted-by-timestamp list, so `get` can binary search for the floor timestamp instead of scanning linearly.

This problem is graded as a sequence of operations: the input is `[actions, values]`, where `actions` names each method call in order and `values` holds its arguments. The result of each `get` call is collected into an array (constructor and `set` calls contribute `null`).
constraints: key and value consist of lowercase English letters and digits
All timestamps of set are strictly increasing for the same key
At most 2 * 10^5 calls will be made to set and get

editorial.approach: Store a Map from key to an array of `[timestamp, value]` pairs, appended in `set()` calls (already sorted since timestamps are strictly increasing per key). In `get()`, binary search that key's array for the rightmost entry whose timestamp is `<= timestamp`; if found, return its value, otherwise return an empty string.
editorial.complexity: O(1) for set, O(log n) for get / O(n) total space
